items.wrong: The room is not clean already.
items.why: Use yet in negative sentences, not already.

items.wrong: The heater no is fixed yet.

teach.goal: Como não traduzir palavra por palavra.
solo: Pergunte por que o erro acontece em português e como evitar.
group: Compare erro e forma natural: The room is not clean already. → The room isn’t clean yet. | The heater no is fixed yet. → The heater isn’t fixed yet. | The towels isn’t dry yet. → The towels aren’t dry yet..
Peça que digam a forma natural em voz alta.
extra90: Cada aluno cria um erro típico seu e o grupo corrige.

errors.w: The room is not clean already.
The heater no is fixed yet.

facts.label: Reclamação educada com yet
facts.sub: Negativo: The room isn’t clean yet. Plural: The towels aren’t dry yet. Pergunta: Is it ready yet? Comece com I’m sorry, but…

facts.label: Ainda não está…
facts.sub: Use isn’t/aren’t + adjetivo + yet para dizer que algo ainda não chegou ao estado esperado: The room isn’t clean yet. The towels aren’t dry yet. Yet fica no fim da frase.

facts.label: Começo educado
facts.sub: Comece com I’m sorry, but… ou Excuse me…: I’m sorry, but the bathroom isn’t clean yet. Isso deixa a reclamação suave e é muito comum em hotéis britânicos e irlandeses.

facts.label: Adjetivos úteis

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Yet is used in negative sentences with still-unfinished things.
We say “The room is not yet clean” only in speaking.
items.why: It is more formal; the usual place of yet is the end.

items.s: “Isn’t ready yet” means it will probably be ready later.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Yet is used in negative sentences with still-unfinished things. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “The room is not yet clean” only in speaking. → Falso (It is more formal; the usual place of yet is the end.)
“Isn’t ready yet” means it will probably be ready later. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A polite complaint at a Dublin hotel · 1/3
paragraphs: It is evening in the center of Dublin. Max has had a long day on trains and buses. He opens the door of his hotel room. The room is untidy, and the bathroom looks wet. Walt, a friend who works at the hotel, meets him in the corridor. Max is tired, but he wants to stay polite.

“Good evening, Max. Is everything all right with your room?” says Walt. “Not really. The room isn’t clean yet, and I am a little tired.” says Max. “I am sorry. The bed isn’t ready yet? I will call the cleaner.” says Walt.
